question.problem: Which of the following gives the area bounded by graph of the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )$, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}$, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 9{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{sin}^{2}⁡(2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{9}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{sin}^{2}⁡(2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
